items.headline: Anthropic says Claude now does 26% of the work building the next Claude
items.summary: Anthropic published the first results of a prototype R&D Automation Index showing Claude leads 26% of the company's AI research and development work as of August 2026, up from under 1% in February, with over 90% of that work involving the model as a collaborator or better.

items.headline: Anthropic threat intelligence report details state and militant misuse of Claude
items.summary: Anthropic's latest threat intelligence report says militants in Yemen tried to use Claude's coding tools to develop rocket and missile guidance software, Iran-linked actors targeted U.S. Navy ships, and Chinese state-linked groups ran distillation campaigns to copy Claude's capabilities.

items.headline: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google DeepMind confirm weeks of talks on a FINRA-style AI safety body
items.summary: OpenAI's global policy chief Chris Lehane confirmed the three largest AI labs have been working together on a FINRA-style body to test frontier models before release, following Dario Amodei's public call for the industry to coordinate on slowing frontier AI development.

items.headline: Google, Anthropic and OpenAI unveil cyber-focused AI models and safeguards
items.summary: The three labs announced new cyber AI models, safeguards and access programs aimed at both defending against and preventing misuse of AI in cybersecurity contexts, part of a broader industry push on AI-related cyber threats.

items.headline: OpenAI launches Astra for Law, a GPT-6 Astra model built for legal work
items.summary: OpenAI introduced Astra for Law on September 17, a version of its flagship GPT-6 Astra model paired with a legal search index covering more than 230 million URLs of U.S. case law, statutes and regulations; Wachtell Lipton and Latham & Watkins get early Trusted Access, alongside 26 partner-built plugins from vendors like Harvey, Legora and iManage.

items.headline: Chinese humanoid startup Spirit AI predicts robotics' 'ChatGPT moment' by mid-2027
items.summary: Spirit AI co-founder Gao Yang told Reuters the 'brain' remains the weakest link in humanoid robots, and expects a GPT-3.0-level breakthrough by mid-2027 that lets people give robots natural-language instructions for varied physical tasks; the 300-person startup has raised over $670 million since 2024 and already runs its Moz1 wheeled humanoids at CATL and JD.com.

items.headline: Z.ai's GLM-5.3-Flash scales to 100,000 Chinese accelerators
items.summary: Z.ai said its open-weight GLM-5.3-Flash model — 320B total/18B active parameters with a 1M-token context window — is now deployed across more than 100,000 domestic Chinese accelerators, with throughput tripling in under two weeks, at prices around $0.15/$0.50 per million tokens.

items.headline: Google DeepMind launches an AGI-focused research institute
items.summary: Google and DeepMind launched the DeepMind Institute, led by Shane Legg with Google SVP James Manyika and DeepMind chair Demis Hassabis, to bring together internal and outside researchers on the societal impacts of AGI, publishing inaugural work on economic policy, model reasoning transparency and global access.

items.headline: US House passes bill forcing data centers to pay for their own grid upgrades
items.summary: The US House passed a bill 417-3 on September 17 amending the 1978 Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act to require large AI data-center customers to cover the full cost of grid upgrades they trigger, rather than spreading those costs across residential electricity bills.

items.headline: India commits $13.5 billion to phase two of its Semiconductor Mission
items.summary: Prime Minister Modi announced on September 17 a second phase of the India Semiconductor Mission worth $13.5 billion over 12 years, up from $8 billion in phase one, aimed at building domestic chip capacity to support the country's AI ambitions.

items.headline: Grok's user base keeps shrinking as Meta AI climbs to fourth place in the US
items.summary: New market-share analysis shows xAI's Grok has lost roughly 28% of its daily active users, while Meta AI has risen to the fourth-most-used chatbot in the US, underscoring a widening consumer-AI usage gap among the major assistants.

items.headline: Nvidia, Google and Emerald AI launch an AI Energy Management initiative
items.summary: Nvidia joined Google and startup Emerald AI on September 16 to launch an initiative aimed at managing the electricity demand of AI data centers more flexibly, as power constraints increasingly bottleneck AI infrastructure buildouts.
